data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Garsenda was a shepherdess who was also a warrior. She protected her flock from danger and led her soldiers into battle. Her name is derived from the Greek words 'agros' meaning countryside and 'hendeia' meaning strength or power. The name Garsenda carries the meaning “Shepherdess of the Army” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Garsenda usually hope their child will grow to embody shepherdess of the army and live with faith, good character and purpose.
